CHEMISTRY
                                               Part B
                                Time—50 minutes
                NO CALCULATORS MAY BE USED FOR PART B.


Answer Question 4 below. The Section II score weighting for this question is 15 percent.

 4. Write the formulas to show the reactants and the products for any FIVE of the laboratory situations described
   below. Answers to more than five choices will not be graded. In all cases, a reaction occurs. Assume that
    solutions are aqueous unless otherwise indicated. Represent substances in solution as ions if the substances are
    extensively ionized. Omit formulas for any ions or molecules that are unchanged by the reaction. You need not
    balance the equations.

   Example: A strip of magnesium is added to a solution of silver nitrate.





    (a) A strip of zinc is placed in a solution of nickel(II) nitrate.

    (b) Solid aluminum hydroxide is added to a concentrated solution of potassium hydroxide.

    (c) Ethyne (acetylene) is burned in air.

    (d) Solid calcium carbonate is added to a solution of ethanoic (acetic) acid.

    (e) Lithium metal is strongly heated in nitrogen gas.

     (f) Boron trifluoride gas is added to ammonia gas.

    (g) Sulfur trioxide gas is bubbled into a solution of sodium hydroxide.

    (h) Equal volumes of 0.1 M solutions of lead(II) nitrate and magnesium iodide are combined.

candidates.name: Oxidation numbers
candidates.definition: Assigning oxidation numbers to atoms and using changes in oxidation number to identify which species are oxidized and reduced and how many electrons transfer.
candidates.include: Tag when oxidation numbers must be assigned or changes in them used.
candidates.exclude: Terms 'oxidizing agent' and 'reducing agent' are not assessed on the current exam; do not confuse with formal charge.

candidates.name: Precipitation reactions
candidates.definition: Predicting whether a precipitate forms when solutions are mixed, using the AP-specified solubility facts (all sodium, potassium, ammonium and nitrate salts are soluble) and given data.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must predict or identify a precipitate qualitatively.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag quantitative Q versus Ksp precipitation tests (tag solubility-product); rote solubility rules beyond the AP-specified cases are not assessed.

candidates.name: Classifying reactions
candidates.definition: Recognizing acid-base, redox (including combustion) and precipitation reactions from equations or observations.
candidates.include: Tag when a reaction must be classified by type or its type is the key to predicting products.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when the type is stated and the question asks only for a calculation.

candidates.name: Brønsted-Lowry acids, bases and conjugate pairs
candidates.definition: Identifying proton donors and acceptors in a reaction, writing conjugate acid-base pairs, and recognizing amphiprotic species such as water.
candidates.include: Tag when acids, bases or conjugate pairs must be identified, or a proton-transfer equation written.
candidates.exclude: Lewis acid-base theory is not assessed.

candidates.name: Net ionic equations
candidates.definition: Writing complete and net ionic equations by dissociating strong electrolytes and removing spectator ions, conserving atoms and charge.
candidates.include: Tag when a net ionic equation must be written or chosen, or spectator ions identified.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when the reaction is only described in words and no ionic representation is required.

candidates.name: Redox half-reactions and balancing
candidates.definition: Writing oxidation and reduction half-reactions, combining them so electrons cancel, and balancing atoms and charge in redox equations.
candidates.include: Tag when half-reactions must be written, combined or balanced, or electron stoichiometry in a redox equation is needed.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag simple oxidation-number assignment (tag oxidation-numbers).

candidates.name: Descriptive reaction prediction
candidates.definition: Recall-based prediction of products for named reaction classes (complex ions, decomposition of specific compounds, flame tests, qualitative analysis schemes) beyond the AP-specified solubility and reaction-type knowledge.
candidates.include: Tag legacy questions that require memorized descriptive chemistry not supported by the current CED.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag predictions that follow from current AP reaction-type reasoning.

candidates.name: Galvanic and electrolytic cells
candidates.definition: Identifying the anode (oxidation) and cathode (reduction), electron flow, salt-bridge ion migration and electrode changes in galvanic and electrolytic cells.
candidates.include: Tag when cell components, half-reactions at each electrode, electron or ion flow, or electrode mass changes must be identified.
candidates.exclude: Assigning + and - labels to electrodes is not assessed; do not tag voltage calculations alone (tag cell-potential).

candidates.name: Solubility equilibria and Ksp
candidates.definition: Writing Ksp expressions, converting between Ksp and molar solubility using formula stoichiometry, comparing solubilities, and predicting precipitation with Q versus Ksp.
candidates.include: Tag when Ksp, molar solubility, or a quantitative precipitation test is used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag qualitative precipitate prediction from solubility facts (tag precipitation).

candidates.name: Acid-base reactions and mixtures
candidates.definition: Determining the products, major species and pH after mixing acids and bases, treating strong-reactant reactions as going to completion and handling the remaining excess or conjugate.
candidates.include: Tag when the composition or pH after mixing an acid and a base must be determined.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag titration-curve interpretation (tag titration-curves) unless a post-mixing calculation is required.

candidates.name: Writing and balancing chemical equations
candidates.definition: Writing balanced chemical equations from descriptions or observations so that atoms are conserved, with correct formulas, coefficients and phases.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must write or balance an equation that is not a net ionic or redox half-reaction equation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a balanced equation is given; use net-ionic-equations or redox-half-reactions for those equation types.

candidates.name: Electrolysis and Faraday's law
candidates.definition: Relating current, time, charge (Q = It), moles of electrons (Faraday constant) and the amount of substance deposited or produced in electrolysis.
candidates.include: Tag when an amount of product, current or time in electrolysis must be calculated.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag qualitative identification of electrodes only (tag electrochemical-cells).

candidates.name: Cell potential and free energy
candidates.definition: Calculating standard cell potential from reduction potentials, relating a positive E°cell to favorability, and using ΔG° = -nFE°.
candidates.include: Tag when E°cell must be calculated or compared, reduction potentials used to rank oxidizing ability, or E° related to ΔG° or K.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag concentration effects on voltage (tag nernst-nonstandard).

candidates.name: Formal charge
candidates.definition: Calculating the formal charge on atoms in a Lewis structure and using formal charges to judge which of several structures best represents a species.
candidates.include: Tag when formal charges must be calculated, compared, or used to choose the preferred structure, even if the words 'formal charge' do not appear.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag oxidation numbers (tag oxidation-numbers) or a Lewis structure question whose answer does not depend on formal charge.

candidates.name: Strong versus weak acids and bases
candidates.definition: Distinguishing strong acids and bases (complete ionization) from weak ones (partial ionization), and separating acid strength from acid concentration.
candidates.include: Tag when an acid or base must be classified as strong or weak, or its extent of ionization represented or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag structure-based strength explanations (tag acid-strength-structure) or Ka calculations (tag weak-acid-equilibrium).

candidates.name: Weak acid and base equilibria (Ka, Kb)
candidates.definition: Writing Ka and Kb expressions, calculating pH or K for weak acid and base solutions, percent ionization, and Ka·Kb = Kw for conjugates.
candidates.include: Tag when Ka, Kb, percent ionization or the pH of a weak acid or base solution must be used or calculated.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag buffer pH calculations (tag henderson-hasselbalch) or titration-curve reading (tag titration-curves).
